title: Your own exception type
description:
Standard exceptions carry only a message. Your own exception class can carry **data** the handler can act on.

1. Write `class InsufficientFunds : public std::runtime_error`. Its constructor takes how many cents were missing; it passes the message `"insufficient funds"` to `std::runtime_error` and remembers the amount. `long long shortBy() const` returns it.
2. Write `class Wallet` with `explicit Wallet(long long cents)`, `long long balance() const`, and `void spend(long long cents)`, which throws `InsufficientFunds` (leaving the balance untouched) if there is not enough.
hints: The exception's constructor passes the message up in its initializer list: `explicit InsufficientFunds(long long missing) : std::runtime_error{ "insufficient funds" }, m_shortBy{ missing } {}`.
In `spend`, check first and throw before changing the balance, so a failed purchase leaves the wallet as it was.
